CHAPTER 1  
INTRODUCTION  
1.1 Introduction 
The landscape of educational technology has significantly evolved over the 
years, from its rudimentary form teaching people how to use software in the 
1980s (Cross, 2004), to the virtual classrooms seen today. The integration of 
technology into the education system has aimed at increasing engagement and 
learning outcomes of students; the affect digital technologies has had on 
education is undeniable. As the technology has enhanced it has addressed 
current issues and concerns, setting the stage for a new challenge. 
The expansive adoption of digital technologies such as social media has 
significantly changed how information is consumed, ultimately leading to a 
decline in the people’s ability to concentrate on longer forms of content (Chen, 
et al., 2022; Gausby, 2015). This poses a unique challenge for educational 
strategies and frameworks; how should teaching methods changed to cater to 
the engagement needs of a generation with a dwindling attention span.  
This project is a direct response to the challenge of declining attention spans 
among GCSE students, by innovating the way in which content is delivered and 
consumed. Central to this project, is the content delivery platform utilising 
short-form videos, to engage students in a format that aligns with modern social 
media consumption habits. These videos will be designed to be concise to ensure 
students receive the information in a way that maximises student retention and 
engagement as supported by (Brame, 2016).
